title: How Does a Seatbelt Know When to Lock?
description:
How does a seatbelt know when to lock? Pull it slowly and it lets you lean forward. Jerk it and it stops dead. There is no chip deciding. Inside the seat belt retractor, a heavy disc that falls behind and a steel ball that keeps going make that call in a split second, with no power at all.

Then the twist: a lock that good can hurt the chest it holds. So in a hard crash your seatbelt makes three moves. A pretensioner snaps it tight, the lock holds, and a torsion-bar load limiter lets it out again, on purpose. How the emergency locking retractor, the seatbelt pretensioner and the load limiter work, why a seatbelt locks when you yank it, and why it sometimes only goes back in (the child-seat mode).
